recap.summary: Week 5 was a 83.3-113.3 loss to St.Brown & Down that dropped us to 1-4 with the league's worst PF (445.28) and worst PA (604.68). The margin was entirely self-inflicted: we started Lamar Jackson (0.0, did not play), Brian Thomas (0.0) and got 4.3 combined from the RB slots, while Justin Jefferson's 17.8 sat on the bench. Isaiah Likely's 32.4 and Jameson Williams' 18.7 were the only things keeping it respectable. The prior packet's biggest failure was roster-management, not projection — a zero at QB and a zero at WR1 is a forfeit in a 9-starter league.
what_worked: Isaiah Likely at TE (32.4) — he is a genuine weekly starter at a scarce position and is now a sell-high asset
Jameson Williams at WR2 (18.7) before his Week 6 bye
Cleveland DEF (13.0) — the streaming-first philosophy is producing; CLE is worth holding another week
what_hurt: Starting Lamar Jackson while he was Out for a 0.0 when Justin Herbert (8.24) was on the bench — unforced error worth roughly 15-20 points
Brian Thomas 0.0 at WR1 while Justin Jefferson scored 17.8 on the bench
RB1/RB2 combined for 4.3 (Allgeier 3.6, Harvey 0.7); the backfield has no reliable volume and Josh Jacobs sat for a zero
recap.self_grade: D — the lineup logic was defensible at TE/DEF but the team left ~35 points on the bench and started a player who was ruled out. That is the difference between 1-4 and 2-3.

waivers.reason: CONDITIONAL — submit this claim only if Saquon Barkley is listed Out or Doubtful on the Friday report; if Barkley is cleared, cancel and keep our #1 priority. Reporting has Pierce taking over as the Eagles' lead back after Will Shipley's foot injury (11 carries in Week 5), and Nick Sirianni has said only that he is 'hopeful' Barkley (hamstring) is cleared. A workhorse Eagles backfield is exactly the 'potential league-winner' the owner authorizes burning priority #1 on, and the drop costs nothing — Bigsby is the IR'd RB4 in that same backfield, so we are converting a dead spot into the live version of the same handcuff. Hamstrings also recur, which keeps Pierce valuable even if Barkley plays Week 6. If an IR slot exists for Bigsby, drop Keaton Mitchell (9511) here instead.

Not worth priority — if it fails, grab him in free agency once waivers clear. This is a Week 7 move made now: next week Brian Thomas (JAX) byes on top of our entire Chargers block (Herbert, Gadsden, Dicker, Mitchell), which would leave us with Jefferson and Burden as the only healthy WRs. Allen is a high-floor, full-route-share slot receiver in a functional Indianapolis offense with a Week 13 bye, so he covers the hole without creating a new one. Mitchell is the right drop because he byes in Week 7 too and is behind Omarion Hampton anyway.

trades.pitch: You're 2-3 with the best RB room in the league (McCaffrey, Judkins, Hubbard, Jaylen Warren, Aaron Jones, Croskey-Merritt, Chris Rodriguez) and you're starting Tyler Shough at QB with no backup. That's a 10-point-a-week hole you can close right now. I'll send Justin Herbert plus Tyler Allgeier for Quinshon Judkins — or Chuba Hubbard if you'd rather keep Judkins. You turn a replacement-level QB slot into a top-five fantasy QB, you keep McCaffrey plus two of Hubbard/Warren/Jones, and you add Allgeier as cover for Arizona's committee. I need the RB, you need the QB — this is the cleanest fit in the league.
trades.why_it_helps_me: Classic 2-for-1 consolidation: it turns our worst starting slot (RB2, 0.7 points last week) into a real workhorse and clears a bench spot. Judkins is a buy-low because he is carrying a Questionable tag right now, and his usage profile holds through the Weeks 14-17 playoff window. Execute only once Lamar Jackson is confirmed back — until then Herbert is our only functioning QB.
trades.why_they_might_accept: They roster seven RBs and literally one QB. Shough is a weekly liability for a team two games out of first; Herbert is a positional upgrade of 8-12 points a week that costs them a back they can't start every week anyway.

trades.pitch: You're 1-4 with 600 points for — you're the unluckiest team in the league and you're one lineup fix from running off six wins. You're starting Kyle Pitts or Brenton Strange at TE while carrying six receivers you can't all play (Evans, Metcalf, McLaurin, Pickens, Doubs, Shaheed). I'll give you Isaiah Likely — he just went for 32.4 as the Giants' every-down TE1 — plus Keaton Mitchell as insurance behind Jeanty and Bijan, for George Pickens (or Terry McLaurin, your choice). You upgrade a starting slot by 10+ a week and lose nothing from your lineup.
trades.why_it_helps_me: We sell Likely at his absolute peak while still owning Oronde Gadsden, the Chargers' TE1, so the TE slot stays filled. In exchange we fix the real problem: with A.J. Brown on IR and Brian Thomas' role in question, our WR corps is one Jefferson injury from unstartable. Pickens/McLaurin is a weekly WR2 with WR1 weeks in it.
trades.why_they_might_accept: They have a genuine WR logjam and the worst starting TE situation among the contenders. At 1-4 with elite point totals they need to maximize every slot now, and TE is where the biggest point swing is available to them.

confidence_notes: Highest-confidence calls: Herbert at QB (forced), Likely at TE, and the two bye-driven benchings. Least certain, in order: (1) Josh Jacobs — live checks show him active with no designation, but he posted a 0.0 in Week 5 and the context flags him oddly, so verify inactives 90 minutes before kickoff; if he's out, Allgeier goes to RB1 and Keaton Mitchell to FLEX. (2) Brian Thomas — he's a start by default with Jefferson and Jameson Williams on bye, but a zero plus a third-string depth listing is a red flag; check the Friday injury report for a shoulder designation. (3) Gadsden over Allgeier in the FLEX is a deliberate ceiling play per the owner's underdog guidance — if the Chargers' game script or a Gadsden practice limitation surfaces, Allgeier is the safe swap. (4) The Pierce claim is explicitly conditional on Barkley's Friday status; do not submit it blind. One process caveat: my live-search budget was exhausted partway through, so the Barkley/Pierce/Shipley reporting and the Week 6 bye slate (CIN, DET, MIN, MIA) are verified, but Cleveland's and Dicker's specific Week 6 matchups and the Chargers'/Jaguars' latest practice reports were not — re-check those Friday before locking. News that would change the packet: Barkley ruled out (submit Pierce claim), Jacobs inactive (RB shuffle above), Lamar cleared (send the mrkw trade immediately), or Brian Thomas picking up a designation (Allen or Burden-plus-Allgeier reshuffle).
